title: Best cities in Indonesia for digital nomads on a budget
summary: Looking for budget-friendly cities in Indonesia? Here are the best cities for digital nomads to live and work easily
body_markdown:
Thinking about working remotely in Indonesia without blowing your budget? Let’s make it easy. I’ll show you cities where you can live comfortably, eat well, and stay productive, all while keeping costs in check.


In this guide, we’ll explore six cities digital nomads love, giving you a taste of the lifestyle, culture, and everyday experiences that make them perfect for more than just working online.


**Also read:**[How to apply for a digital nomad visa in Indonesia](http://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-indonesia)


## **Top digital nomad cities to live in Indonesia**


### Bali


If you’re a freelancer chasing balance, Bali fits the dream. You’ll find strong Wi-Fi, co-working hubs in Canggu and Ubud, and plenty of affordable rooms from Rp 3–5 million a month. Lunch at a local warung costs less than a coffee in London. Between projects, you can surf, join a community event, or just work from a café overlooking rice fields. Work feels lighter here.


### Surabaya


Surabaya is Indonesia’s second-largest city, offering a mix of modern infrastructure and local charm. Reliable public transport and numerous cafés make working remotely straightforward. Accommodation is cheaper than in Bali, with decent apartments in central districts. Street food and local markets make living costs manageable. When you’re done with work, you can explore colonial architecture, parks, and cultural landmarks, experiencing city life without the crowds of Jakarta.


### Bandung


Bandung’s cooler climate makes it appealing for long working days. Cafés with strong Wi-Fi and creative co-working spaces are scattered throughout the city. Rent and food costs are lower than in Jakarta, and local transport is cheap. You can explore art galleries, nearby volcanic landscapes, and coffee plantations during downtime. The city balances affordable living with a vibrant, youthful atmosphere, perfect if you want a mix of work and leisure.


### Yogyakarta


Yogyakarta feels like home from the moment you arrive. You’ll find affordable living, about Rp 3 million covers rent and meals, and a warm, welcoming community of artists and freelancers. Internet is reliable, co-working spaces are friendly, and the city’s cultural heart keeps you grounded. After work, wander Malioboro Street or catch a sunset near Prambanan Temple. It’s calm, creative, and full of heart.


**Also read:**[Indonesia for remote workers: tips, connectivity, and community](http://grey.co/blog/indonesia-for-remote-workers-tips-connectivity-and-community)


### Jakarta


In Jakarta, almost everyone and everything is moving fast. Freelancers here enjoy modern co-working hubs, quick Wi-Fi, and countless networking opportunities. Costs are higher, but so are possibilities. You can live modestly in areas like Kemang or Tebet, eat great food at every corner, and hop on the MRT to avoid traffic. It’s busy, yes, but full of energy and connection.


### Denpasar


Denpasar gives you local life with modern comfort. Rent is affordable, Wi-Fi is stable, and you’re only a short ride from Bali’s beaches. You’ll find freelancers working from home, cafés, or small co-working spaces, with living costs around Rp 5 million a month. Evenings are peaceful, filled with local food stalls and friendly faces. It’s a steady base for freelancers who value calm and connection.
